clue.text: Religion in spirit could be 23 or 16 across, or 10 or 19

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: a fay is a fairy, a small magical spirit
a cult is a religious sect or form of worship

explanation.surface: A musing that religious spirit might take the form of various human abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references give ARTS, SCIENCE, SIGHT and HEARING: two university divisions and two of the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Arts and science are university departments called faculties, while sight and hearing are bodily powers, the other sense of the word.

clue.text: Female goes to jug - there aren't that many

indicators.note: one thing going to another means the second follows straight after the first

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for female
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A woman heads for the jug, and finds it nearly empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a number is smaller is the same as saying there are not so many of something.

clue.text: Talk to attractive little baby on the nail

definitions.note: a phrase for the noun: the thing found on the nail

indicators.note: talk signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: attractive is cute, and ickle is the baby-talk way of saying little

explanation.surface: Cooing over a sweet infant, perhaps right on the button.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the nail' reads like an idiom for 'exactly', but it is literal: the skin at the base of a fingernail.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the thin strip of hardened skin at the base and edge of a fingernail or toenail.

clue.text: Spring appeared this February?

blocks.note: surface reading: some springlike event happened early, in February
setter's reading: spring as a jump, in a February of a leap year (this was 2000), with F for February replacing the final letter, and also the new growth seen in spring

explanation.surface: An early spring, arriving in February this year.
explanation.walkthrough: February 2000 had 29 days, so it was a leap February; swap the last letter of LEAP for F (February) and you also have the new growth of spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is the green growth that appears on trees in spring, and a leap year adds a day to February.

clue.text: Never mind the millennium: this is how to foregather on day

indicators.note: 'how to' make something implies the following letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used as the raw material

explanation.surface: Forget the new millennium; this is the occasion to gather on the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared early in 2000, when the Chinese year beginning in February was the Dragon's, a rival celebration to the millennium.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Chinese calendar the year starting February 2000 was assigned to the dragon, so it was this year's other identity.

clue.text: Polish article - name, a roll?

blocks.note: to polish is to rub
the indefinite article
to dub is to name

explanation.surface: A furniture-polish product and its name, sold as a roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' disguises itself with a capital, as if it meant from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Rub-a-dub imitates the beating of a drum, so it stands for a drum roll.

clue.text: OK for lord to keep posh artist in the cabinet?

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

blocks.note: right-ho is a cheery British way of saying OK
a lord is a noble
U means upper-class in British usage
Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Is it all right for a peer to hire a smart painter in government?
explanation.walkthrough: Right-ho is breezy British slang; U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's essays. RA means a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinet ministers are Privy Counsellors, who carry the title of Right Honourable before their names.

clue.text: A way for poet to go round pub with sinister band

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: a bard is a poet
A plus ST, the abbreviation for street
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A path for a poet to walk around a pub, alongside a menacing band.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet surrounds the A ST. In heraldry, a band drawn on the sinister side of a coat of arms marks illegitimacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastard bar is a heraldic stripe on the left, sinister, side of the shield, signifying illegitimate descent.

clue.text: Stalk a celebrity, the brightest of the lot

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them persistently
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: Pursue a famous person, the most dazzling of them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: Crazy fellow who doesn't want to get out

definitions.text: who doesn't want to get out

blocks.note: bats is slang for mad
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A mad man who refuses to leave the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting player is 'out' when dismissed, so he wants to stay in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer at the crease tries to avoid dismissal, which in the game is called getting out.

clue.text: How things began - well - but won't end?

blocks.note: first meaning: the universe started in the Big Bang
second meaning: an idiom for successfully and impressively
surface padding: a nod to Eliot's line about how the world ends

explanation.surface: The universe started brilliantly, but the poet says it won't finish that way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But won't end' recalls T. S. Eliot's 'The Hollow Men': the world ends 'not with a bang but a whimper'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos began with an explosion, and doing something successfully and spectacularly is also described with this idiom.

clue.text: Express regret at model spectacle

blocks.note: to sigh is to express sorrow
Ford's Model T

explanation.surface: Groaning with disappointment at a fashion model's show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is something worth seeing, a remarkable display or view.

clue.text: See 22
Afterbirth? You need support - mat, possibly

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'after birth'; the noun reading is the misdirection

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among others, so the letters can be reordered

blocks.note: both words supply letters

explanation.surface: Advice to a new mother: you need a supportive mat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afterbirth' looks like the placenta, but split it into 'after birth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived adjective describes the period following childbirth.

clue.text: Name for male creature left in peace, one of many 12

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: peace is quiet
abbreviation for name
a tup is a ram
abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A name for a male animal left in peace, one of a big litter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is a British dialect word for a ram; the 12 refers to the after-birth answer at 12-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of five babies born at one birth is one of a multiple set of newborns.

clue.text: Before the previous month, engineers outcome

indicators.note: one thing coming before another fixes which part is written first

blocks.note: REs, members of the Royal Engineers, in the plural
ult., ultimo, is old business-letter shorthand for last month

explanation.surface: Engineers report their findings ahead of last month's figures.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army, abbreviated RE; here pluralised to mean the engineers themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the consequence or end product of some process.

clue.text: It's probably not steam and possibly not electric

definitions.text: It's probably not steam and possibly not electric

blocks.clueFragment: It's probably not steam and possibly not electric
blocks.note: surface reading: a railway engine or a train powered by neither
setter's reading: a household pressing appliance of the vintage kind, heated on a stove rather than by steam or electricity

explanation.surface: Guessing about a locomotive that is neither steam nor electric.
explanation.walkthrough: Steam and electric suggest trains, but they also describe the household appliances for pressing clothes; the antique metal kind is neither.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal, or a vintage flat-iron heated on the stove, needs no steam and no electricity.

clue.text: It employs induction differently in unlubricated c-coil, see?

indicators.note: without lubrication means the oil is taken away
arranged differently means the letters take another order

blocks.note: taken as written
remove OIL from coil, leaving C, next to the first C
taken as written

explanation.surface: An electrical coil that needs oil behaves differently under induction, see?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Induction' sounds electrical, but the definition means inductive reasoning, from evidence to general law.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientific method reasons by induction, drawing general laws from observed particular instances.

clue.text: Tommy's upset about piano, which must mean something

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disordered
about means surrounding, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of the name and its s
musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A boy is distressed about his piano, and it must signify something.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign indicating a disease or condition, so it signifies something beyond itself.

clue.text: Stately home for princess?

blocks.note: at home is in
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: Would a grand country house suit a royal princess?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stately home' is a British phrase for an aristocratic country house, but split it: 'stately' points to a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, so it is a thing that is a state.

clue.text: It comes in for a cheap alternative to spinach

indicators.note: coming in means sitting within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A budget substitute for spinach is arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Orache, or mountain spinach, is a leafy plant cooked as a vegetable in place of spinach.

clue.text: Audition not just for the bride these days?

definitions.text: not just for the bride these days

blocks.note: first meaning: the sense or act of listening

blocks.clueFragment: not just for the bride these days
blocks.note: second meaning, split differently: he gets a ring too now, as grooms wear wedding bands

explanation.surface: A tryout no longer reserved for brides in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as HE A RING: modern grooms wear a wedding ring too.
explanation.definitionFit: Audition is a formal word for the faculty of perceiving sound, and a hearing is also a trial session.

clue.text: Spiritualist of unusual quality's not well done

blocks.note: a medium contacts the spirits
rare means uncommon and fine

explanation.surface: A psychic of exceptional talent has done a poor job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well done' reads as a criticism but is a steak order.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked between rare and medium is pink inside, so it is cooked less than well done.

clue.text: Half-Polynesian garment of liquid 11

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the rest dropped

blocks.note: a lava-lava is a wraparound skirt worn in Samoa and elsewhere in Polynesia

explanation.surface: Half a South Seas wrap made of fluid stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lava is molten stone flowing from a volcano, which cools into solid stone.

clue.text: Monolithic philosopher's music?

definitions.note: adjective for the noun: the answer is a monolith

blocks.note: A. J. Ayer, the British logical positivist philosopher
rock music

explanation.surface: A philosopher's tunes are as massive as a single stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Uluru in central Australia is a huge sandstone monolith, a single standing rock mass.

clue.text: Skills mastered by the 9

blocks.note: surface reading: abilities that a certain nine people have learned
setter's reading: the nine Muses, goddesses who preside over creative pursuits, and a Master holds a degree in them

explanation.surface: Abilities perfected by a group of nine.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9-across, but it is the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, poetry, music and the rest are creative skills, each under the protection of a Muse.

clue.text: The way to be behind

blocks.note: first meaning: a path or track
second meaning: to lag or be losing

explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a marked track through country, and to trail is to lag behind rivals in a contest.

clue.text: Talk a lot to the queen and make a meal of the material

blocks.note: to gab is to chatter
the article taken as A, plus R for Regina
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Chattering away to Her Majesty and making a fuss over the fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a meal of' is an idiom for overdoing something, but here it is split between DINE and the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabardine is a tightly woven twill fabric used for raincoats and suits.

clue.text: Singular church service including point for Sunday dinner?

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside

blocks.note: the morning office, Mattins, made singular by losing its S
east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A lone church service with a pointed message for Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Mattins is the Anglican spelling of the morning service. The traditional British Sunday dinner is a roast joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting tray is what the Sunday joint of beef or lamb cooks in.

clue.text: Flag officers?

definitions.note: singular here; the answer is plural

blocks.note: first meaning: a ship's national flags
second meaning: junior commissioned ranks in the US Navy, once also army standard-bearers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag officers' is a real term for admirals, which is the trap; split it into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means banners flown by ships and also the lowest commissioned naval officers.
